An unmarked sentence of a normative section reads as MUST.
The view depends only on the bytes of the manifest and the standard files of chapter 2.1 (the schema\n`02.1-installer.schema.json`, the layer table `02.1-installer.layers.tsv`).
- `sugar` is a closed list of reductions to one form, applied before defaults.
- `sugar.bound_to`: for a unit field and a table field, a single name `"x"` becomes `["x"]`.
- `sugar.in`: for an element of `secret_in` of the regex kind, a single word `"query"` becomes `["query"]`.
- `defaults`: an absent section without default stays absent.
- `ordered`: other maps are objects; their order is JCS.
- `ordered`: a reader does not rely on author order outside `ordered`.
- `form` is the number of the view form, a decimal integer ≥ 1; now 1 (key `…/canonical/1`).
- `rev` is the rev of the manifest row `platform/manifest/<sub>` from which the view is built (chapter 2.3 N1.5).
- `sha256` is the sha256 of the manifest row (its field `sha256`).
- `manifest` is the bytes of the view (N1.1) as text — JCS, UTF-8, without a final newline.

- `ceiling`: its source is the actual ceiling of the store: `max_value` of the answer of `GET /v1/status` (P/01.3 N2,\n  OpenAPI 01 `StatusResponse`); 524288 is only the default of the daemon flag `-max-value`, not a constant of the\n  installer; the installer has no ceiling setting of its own.
- `window`: during the change window the installer writes both forms.
- The view schema is closed where the form is.
- In the view schema, keys with `default` are required.
The chapter has no doors of its own.
`rev` is the final new rev chosen by the caller (chapter 2.3 N3 step 14a), not an earlier estimate.
On `toolarge` of the view, refuse the whole\n   installation: nothing is written, exit code 2; stderr names the file, the view key, the weight and the ceiling.
A `cas` conflict that changes the new rev repeats this check before any further write.
5. If the view is not written because of a `cas` conflict, re-read the row and the view:
1. If the rev of the row is mine, repeat the `cas` of the view.

2. If the rev of the row is already another one (another installer wrote a newer one), run the procedure again from\n      reading the row (my file — a new rev or «unchanged»; a new rev — with the weight check of item 2 for that rev).
The view of the former rev is not written: the view always carries the rev of the current row.
1. Read the mark, then the view of its own form.
An unconfirmed read of the mark or of the view (the store did not answer) is repeated the same way.

If they still do not match at the end of `START_WAIT`: the refusal «not published» — do not start, exit code 1; the supervisor\n   restarts the process (the temporary outcome of chapter 2.3 N3 «Process start»).
While the reader repeats, it serves nothing.
